Both sets are RATCHETS over a measured population, not licences: the guard asserts them in BOTH directions, so an entry whose file has stopped offending reds the guard until the entry is deleted. The write set pins a MULTISET of licensed destinations — pinning only the count let three legitimate fixture writes be SUBSTITUTED for three `tests/*.tmp.ts` writes, and pinning only the destinations let a licensed write be DUPLICATED, both with the guard still green. The leak set pins counts per file, so a new leak inside an already-listed file reds too.

packages/kn-next/src/__tests__/adapter-d.reason: Boots a REAL `next dev` server. `next` resolves ITS OWN dist modules by walking cwd's ancestor directories for `node_modules/next` (#1658 round 2) — an `os.tmpdir()` copy has no such ancestor and `next dev` fails closed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. So the live-run copy (`workDir`, a fresh sibling of the tracked `fixtures/dev-edge-fence/` template) has to sit inside `packages/kn-next/`, whose `node_modules` the ancestor walk then finds. `workDir` is created with `mkdirSync`/`cpSync`, never `mkdtempSync` (#1658 round 3): `mkdtemp`'s own half of this guard has no exception mechanism at all — every `mkdtemp` call must literally name `tmpdir`/`TMP`, unconditionally — so an in-repo scratch directory has to go through THIS licence instead, on the write half, which is the mechanism #918 provides for exactly this case. `cpSync(FIXTURE, workDir, {recursive:true})` populates `workDir` FROM the tracked, read-only fixture (never the reverse — `FIXTURE` itself is asserted unchanged after every run); `writeFileSync(join(workDir, ".knext", ".gitignore"))` marks the generated adapter bundle as never-committed. Not the #918 shape either: nothing here writes a transient `.ts` into `tests/`, which is what raced the typecheck gate. `mkdirSync(dirname(adapterBundle))` and `mkdirSync(typesDir)` (also inside `workDir`) are not listed here because the scan does not see them as repo-rooted at all — they resolve through one more layer of local-variable indirection than the scan's identifier-resolution depth budget (3 hops) follows, so it reports them `unknown` rather than `repo` (fail-open by design); listing them here would itself red "every licensed write still exists", since the scan never finds a live match to consume. The licence is these two EXPRESSIONS: any other destination in this file, including one substituted for one of these, is a red.

unremovedTempDirs.note: Unremoved `mkdtemp` sites, measured when the LIFETIME half of this guard landed (D9): originally 157 across 47 files. Burn-down tracked in #939 — the first pass paired 35 sites across 30 files with an `rmSync`, leaving 122 across 17 files; a later pass burned 122 down to 92 across 8 files by pairing 30 more sites across 9 files (bench scripts, `verify-action-pins`, and the storage/native/usage/prewarm/sbom specs) with a try/finally, an `afterAll`/`afterEach` drain over a registry, or a direct removal. Each pairing shrank this ceiling in the SAME change that fixed it, because the guard reds a file that stopped leaking but stayed on the list. The remainder is deferred, not licensed: fixing every site means touching files across every package, and a guard that lands with its subject already red teaches people to disable it. This list is a CEILING: a file may only leak fewer than it does today, never more, and a file that stops leaking must leave the list. Nothing may be added to it — a new leak is a red, including a new leak in a file already here and a new leak that reuses a binding name already here. That last clause was FALSE when it was first written: a leak whose name collided with a drained iteration's loop element rode free, because that loop's own `rmSync(d)` was counted a second time as a direct removal. Measured against the pre-fix scan by appending a probe leak under each loop-element name: 12 (file, name) pairs, of which 8 were closed by excluding drain bodies from direct credit and 4 more needed that exclusion widened to loops over a non-identifier iterable (`of [appDir]`, `of dirs.splice(0)`). 0 remain. The guard proves the claim on the colliding name rather than on a name chosen to pass.
